title: A lower-bound conjecture for the tripartite nullity
statement:
Let $V_1,V_2,V_3$ be the local qudit vector spaces with dimensions $d_1,d_2,d_3$, and let $n_a$ be the corresponding one-party nullities. For a tripartite state $v\in V_1\otimes V_2\otimes V_3$, let $n_{1,2,3}$ denote the nullity of the common kernel space $K_{1,2,3}(v)$. **The tripartite-nullity lower-bound conjecture.** The nullity $n_{1,2,3}$ satisfies

$$
n_{1,2,3}\ge\max\bigl\{(d_{1}d_{2}-d_{3}+n_{3})n_{3},(d_{1}d_{3}-d_{2}+n_{2})n_{2},(d_{2}d_{3}-d_{1}+n_{1})n_{1}\bigr\}.
$$

The authors report extensive empirical evidence for this lower bound, which is intended to improve the available estimates for the invariant controlling tripartite entanglement classes; its general validity remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10728

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).
source_name: Roman V. Buniy and Thomas W. Kephart, “Tripartite entanglement of qudits”, arXiv:2412.10728 (2024).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A reader-posted argument claims a complete proof of the conjecture, but it has not been independently checked, so the result is not settled.
progress.summary:
Buniy and Kephart proposed the conjecture in December 2024: the common-kernel nullity should exceed an explicit maximum determined by the dimensions and one-party nullities.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10728)*

**Known results**

The authors report extensive empirical evidence, but state that they have only upper and lower bounds for $n_{1,2,3}$ and no complete result.


**Posted attempt**

A reader claims a complete proof by showing, for each permutation $(i,j,k)$, that $K_i(v)\otimes\ker f_{j,k}(v)\subseteq K_{1,2,3}(v)$; dimension counting then gives each term in the conjectured maximum. The argument has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture has a complete-proof claim based on an unverified reader argument; no independently corroborated proof or counterexample is recorded.

*Caveats. The posted argument may contain an unrecognized issue, so the conjecture should be treated as open pending verification.*

solutions.body:
Let \(v\in V_1\otimes V_2\otimes V_3\), put \(d_i=\dim V_i\), \(n_i=\dim K_i(v)\), and set \(r_i=d_i-n_i\). Thus \(r_i\) is the rank of the \(i\)-th flattening of \(v\).

For each permutation \((i,j,k)\) of \((1,2,3)\), the two-party contraction
\[
f_{j,k}(v):V_j\otimes V_k\longrightarrow V_i^*
\]
has rank \(r_i\), and hence
\[
\dim\ker f_{j,k}(v)=d_jd_k-r_i.
\]

For \(u\in K_i(v)\) and \(z\in\ker f_{j,k}(v)\), the tensor \(u\otimes z\) belongs to the common kernel \(K_{1,2,3}(v)\). Indeed, the \((j,k)\)-contraction vanishes because \(z\in\ker f_{j,k}(v)\), and each of the other two pair contractions vanishes because \(u\in K_i(v)\). Consequently,
\[
K_i(v)\otimes\ker f_{j,k}(v)\subseteq K_{1,2,3}(v),
\]
so
\[
n_{1,2,3}(v)\geq n_i(d_jd_k-r_i)
=n_i(d_jd_k-d_i+n_i).
\]

Taking the maximum over \(i=1,2,3\) gives precisely the asserted lower bound for every tripartite tensor, including the zero tensor.
